correctness.rationale: Both frozen and narrowed variance statements are mathematically correct. In normal form, the two orientation classes give shortest squared lengths min(4a²,b²) and a²+dist(2y,bZ)². The fundamental rectangle has area ab, and folding a uniform position modulo b gives the asserted uniform D, CDF and two cap transitions. Integrating on the uncapped interval and adding the capped mass gives the stated moments and variance normalization 1/(4s). Inserting v=√3s at the first cap gives the cubic; strict Jensen puts its unique positive stationary point inside that regime. Beyond the cap the original comparison is valid by contraction of pairwise differences; the repaired text verifies this directly via L_t=min(1,√(L_s²+t²−s²)) with the same D. This map is Lipschitz with constant at most (1+t²−s²)^(−1/2)<1 on [0,1], so the pairwise formula strictly decreases the positive variance for s<1. Positivity there follows by varying D in a small uncapped interval; s≥1 is degenerate. Independent numerical evaluation gave s*=0.24009981141289302 and W*=0.007976414224378097, only a rounding check. The uploaded checker was inspected, not run; all-real conclusions follow analytically. The corrected RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt were checked against these derivations.

value.rationale: Area normalization gives a genuine comparison across flat metrics rather than across arbitrary sizes. The exact constant and unique shape identify where local short-loop geometry is most heterogeneous; the strict comparison beyond the first transition is needed to certify global, not merely local, sharpness. Spatial heterogeneity is a different question from minimizing the shortest loop or maximizing a pointwise radius. The repaired claim omits routine pushforward novelty while preserving this motivated extremal result.
